title: Indexing a time-major list
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $k,N,j\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\to\alpha$. If $j<kN$, then the entry at index $j$ of the list formed by concatenating, for each $t<N$ in order, the list $f(t,0),\ldots,f(t,k-1)$ is $f(\lfloor j/k\rfloor,j\bmod k)$.
replaced: For every element family on times and tapes, tape count $k$, bound $N$, and index $j < kN$, the $j$-th entry of the list enumerating, for each time below $N$, the $k$ tape entries in order, is the entry at time $j$ divided by $k$ and tape $j$ modulo $k$; the zero-tape case has no legal index.
